subject: Music Production
title: The Economics of Sample Clearance
description: A 60-second lesson on The Economics of Sample Clearance.

hook.text: Clearing a sample requires negotiating with both the songwriter and the owner of the recording.

buildup.text: Costs range from a few thousand dollars to hundreds of thousands, depending on the sample's fame.

discovery.text: Some owners demand a percentage of the new song's royalties on top of the upfront clearance fee.

twist.text: Independent artists often cannot afford clearance, so they avoid sampling or risk legal action.

climax.text: The high cost of clearance has fundamentally changed which producers can afford to sample freely.

punchline.text: A two-bar loop can cost more than the whole album.

quiz.question: Who must be contacted to clear a sample?
options: Both the songwriter and the recording owner
